subject: Commit lifecycle proposal: stepped monthly uplift, tier reband & invoice timing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan@quickcart.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Commit lifecycle proposal: stepped monthly uplift, tier reband & invoice timing

Hi Ethan / Lynn,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick follow-up with a concrete proposal to get QuickCart aligned to the next usage band while keeping cost predictability. Attached: "commit-amendment-draft.pdf" and oct usage snapshot "usage-report-oct2026.csv".

Summary (proposed):
- Stair-step commit ladder: 3-month ramp (Dec/Jan/Feb) from 1.5B tokens/month -> 2.5B -> 3.5B; final steady-state at 3.5B.
- Ratebands: introduce tiered per-token pricing at each step (details in PDF).
- Soft-throttle and burst: 10% monthly burst pocket for first 90 days; soft-throttle threshold at 120% of current commit to avoid sudden job failures.
- Invoice timing and proration: monthly invoicing in arrears; first invoice prorated for Dec partial month if we enable mid-month.
- Ops: canary rollout window + telemetry hooks; recommended provisioning date: 2026-12-06.

Action items for QuickCart:
1) Confirm acceptance of the staged commit ladder and burst pocket by 2026-11-10.
2) Legal: review and redline the attached amendment.
3) Billing: confirm invoicing preference (net-30 vs net-45).

If those look good I can send the redline-ready version to QuickCart Legal and push the DocuSign envelope. We can also include an explicit SLA credit schedule in Appendix A if you want it called out.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: commit-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: usage-report-oct2026.csv (CSV)]

Subject: Re: Commit lifecycle proposal: stepped monthly uplift, tier reband & invoice timing

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we escalate to legal: 

- Burst pockets: will overage past the burst be charged at the next tier rate or billed as overage at list? Can you call that out in the amendment?
- SLA credits: can we get a simple table (latency/availability) that maps to credits? Our ops team needs that to justify the uplift.
- Invoice timing: we prefer monthly in arrears with net-30. Any chance the first invoice can be deferred by 7 days to align with our existing billing cadence?

Also copying our legal lead Lynn to start the review.

—Ethan

Date: 2026-11-03T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Commit lifecycle proposal — redline & next steps

Folks — attaching a redlined amendment (commit-amendment-redline.pdf) and a short summary of changes. Please review and confirm so I can circulate the DocuSign envelope.

Redline highlights: 
- Explicit callout on burst handling: overage after the burst pocket will be billed at the agreed-up next-step per-token rate (clarified language).
- SLA credit table added to Appendix A (credits capped at 10% of monthly invoice).
- Payment: standard net-30. First invoice can be deferred by 7 days per Karthik's note; we will reflect that in the DocuSign cover sheet.
- Data residency: clarified that QuickCart production data remains in the customer-specified region; logs/audit exports as per the SOC 2 schedule.
- Soft-throttle window: tightened wording to allow up to two automated soft-throttle events per billing period before manual remediation steps.

Next steps: 
1) QuickCart legal to confirm or further redline by EOD 2026-11-10.
2) Marissa to confirm provisioning date and whether QuickCart wants the canary earlier.
3) Karthik/Naomi to confirm OPS ticket and capacity reservation.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/quickcart/tx/ABC123-sign

Thanks — Steph
